root_cause.text: `mtd_parser_tplink_safeloader_parse()` in the MTD TP-Link SafeLoader parser had an error-handling path that freed `parts[idx].name` but forgot to free the temporary table buffer `buf` allocated by `mtd_parser_tplink_safeloader_read_table()`, causing a memory leak when `parts[idx].name` allocation failed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `kfree(buf);` at the `err_free` label, and the CVE description explicitly says `buf` is allocated by `mtd_parser_tplink_safeloader_read_table()` and leaked when the code jumps to `err_free` after a failed `parts[idx].name` allocation.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in `mtd_parser_tplink_safeloader_parse()`. The function allocates a temporary table buffer with `buf = mtd_parser_tplink_safeloader_read_table(mtd);` and later, on name-allocation failure, jumps to `err_free:` where it only frees previously duplicated partition names: `for (idx -= 1; idx >= 0; idx--) kfree(parts[idx].name);`. There is no `kfree(buf)` on this error path, even though `buf` is only freed on the successful path (`kfree(buf);` before returning). This matches the root cause: if `parts[idx].name = kstrdup(name, GFP_KERNEL);` fails, `buf` leaks. The fix is not present in this snippet because the error label does not release `buf` before returning.
